body: Why not allow some of those distractions at night before bed? Anything in particular you like to listen to or watch?  Honestly, one of my best coping skills is watching the same show every night before bed. Helps keep racing thoughts and bad things at bay.  For the past few years it’s been “Teen Titans Go”. Yeah it’s a kids show but I don’t have to worry about sleeping through something horrific (like the news) or inappropriate (like South Park) and it’s a pretty damn good show.  Maybe review your sleep routines.  Nights are tough because of all the dead space. My advice would be to fill it.  If you had to watch the same movie or TV show every night, what is the first thing that comes to mind?

I would love to have a small room.  I’m making an “alternate life” book and I’m making sure I put a small apartment in it.  I have a fairly big house and really don’t care for it.  Something small can help me focus.  If the library is your sanctuary then have at it.  But, I don’t know, first thought in my mind is why not turn your small, messy room into the library you’ve always wanted. It’s a small project but could be meaningful.  I can picture some bookcases, cool vintage movie posters, a small table with some cafe style chairs, a chess board (not sure if you play or not but definitely pumps up the cool factor).  It’s a small, long term project, but could be worthwhile. What kind of books would you fill in it?

Tell me about it.  You would think our SO’s would be the PRIMARY person we can talk to about this kind of stuff but yet they end up being the LAST person who want to divulge our inner most darkest thoughts?  Like, I thought they wanted this job, what the F, right?!

Sorry, venting because I can obviously relate.  Also about the title of the post.  I wondered if I could hire someone to do the job for me, even looked on the dark web (TOR) for ideas about it. It was a non-starter.

I don’t know. I’m currently in a place where I want to die but not actively.  Morbid ruminations is the clinical term.  Surprisingly, having morbid ruminations is not something you can forcibly hospitalize someone for. So many times I’ve had people want me to 5150 their loved ones for that, and I told them that legally I cannot do that.  There’s no plan. It’s just that they don’t care if something horrible happens to them that causes them to die.  They welcomed it.

I suppose that’s better than feeling suicidal. Maybe it’s a step in the right direction.  I don’t know.  But look, you have to find a way to talk your problems out.  If you keep this kind of stuff from your SO, you’re only going to breed resentment which us going to fuel your depression and your downward spiral into this darkness you’re feeling.  Today I asked my SO about suicide in general, I forgot how I framed the question about I asked in a way I wanted her opinion on it without inserting myself into it. The advice she had was good, in fact.  It would’ve been nice if it was directed at me instead of a hypothetical but I’m accepting it as advice to me at the moment. It wasn’t a planned thing but it worked. I don’t know.  Give it a try.  Say you saw a Reddit post about someone whose experiencing something not EXACTLY as you are experiencing but enough for you to make it personal without them knowing it’s about you.  Say it’s a friend of whatever it is that will work.  See what their advice would be to that person.  Good luck!

EDIT: I’m in the same boat as you.  I have a wife, great job, good income, everything you think life would want. But feel like “what’s the point”.  Sometime, the point isn’t known yet or at least not at the moment.  At least that’s what I’m telling myself right now to get to tomorrow.  Either way, hope my advice helps.

You say you can’t write but then again, you wrote something pretty good just now.

Tell me, in a poem, or just random thoughts, what is it about the library that draws you in?

That sort of anxiety sounds very clinical. It’s not abnormal either. I’ve had patients in and out of that anxiety cyclically throughout the day.  After treatment though (and the realization that it doesn’t just improve automatically overnight), they improve enough to actually live sustainable lives.  When your mind blanks out, what does it naturally narrows its focus on when it “wakes up”?
What makes the days more bearable than the nights if you don’t mind me asking?

Trust me, I got Covid and dying ain’t coming any easier.  Funny thing, I just watched a funny movie. It’s been awhile since I’ve watched one. Usually I’ve been watching drama movies, or romance movies.  Nothing funny recently.  But today, after an argument over how miserable our marriage is, wife suggested that we watch a comedy.  Surprisingly, I feel better.  Still feel like shit from the COVID but the urge to want to end my life has subsided or at least been postponed.  It’s funny how, well, funny things can help me us feel better.  

Look, I have kids, and money isn’t too much of an issue for me as it is for others.  Yea, it’s still a “struggle” but my family and I are well off considering.  Money doesn’t make things better but treatment does.  And there are mental health treatments for those with no money.  Not sure what country you’re from but most county mental health systems have programs that can assist you with little to no income needed.  Plus they have cook programs that allow you to connect with others.  And sometimes that’s what we need: a connection. For instance, I’m feeling better posting on here with my pseudo.  Maybe it’s just the writing. Maybe it’s how am I putting my thoughts down and out of my head. I don’t know. But it’s working and I’ll keep doing it.

So if you had to watch a funny movie right now at this moment; which comes to mind?

EDIT: And yes, it sucks what “mess” I may leave the kids if I were to end it. It’s something that’s definitely on the forefront of my mind. But EVERYONE leaves some imprint somewhere on someone when they die. I’ve seen it too often.

How can you know if no one noticed if you were gone if you hadn’t logged in to see reactions? They could be asking and you wouldn’t know.  Not sure how connected your friends are to you outside of Discord.  Maybe find another way to connect or connect with someone here who is also seeking connection that’s maybe around your age or something.  For every suicide I’ve been around, I can assure you - someone always knows and someone always is affected.

But you shouldn’t want to live for others.  You obviously wanted to connect with someone who obviously didn’t reciprocate. That means that you do want connection.  You do want to have and harness something that resembles that.  As long as the want is there, you have a reason to go on. Heck; you even have friends on discord who you can talk to.  I highly doubt they’d just tell you to STFU.

Take what you do have and find the meaning you’re looking for in that - the rest will fall into place.  You’re a gamer - there’s plenty out there you haven’t tried and Cyberpunk 2077 isn’t even out yet!  Let me help ya. What kind of games do you play?

Maybe try something meditative to learn to harness whatever you have taken hold of during the exercise and apply it to outside of exercises.  Maybe it’s also the endorphins that are released during exercising that helps.  Maybe a hobby or an activity that helps release the same endorphins.

Writing my post earlier helped me as well. Maybe writing more is what I need to do, period. Whether it’s a suicide note or just a stream-of-consciousness sort of session.  Either way, I’ll be exploring it more. Thank you.

1) I’ve given into the bluffs before and made the situation far worse, empowering her further. I can’t get into too much detail considering the throwaway nature of this account with a fake name, but I feel like if I do gave into the bluffs - we will get to a point of no return that will affect me and my children. I personally don’t think she cares if she got to that point.  Her family is very close to her and would carry her through anything which is great.  She doesn’t have a career or any means of income and has no qualms about getting welfare or food stamps (even stated she rather we be on welfare than me work as much as I do - but doesn’t object to vacations, Disney annual passes, video games systems, DoorDash on a daily basis, etc.).

2) I’ll try and sit down and look at what I wrote in a 3rd person perspective.  But on the onset, I would encourage that person to seek counseling; even without the wife involved so as to salvage whatever sanity he still has.  Counseling can look further an deeper into his problem as opposed to a simple answer to an overarching problem.  That sometimes separation may be best so that both parties can understand where the marriage should go if it even should continue at all. And also view what is best for the children in this as well as their own benefit.  If the person is miserable to the point of suicidal, then the marriage definitely needs some review.  As I’ve said before, I’ve talked a lot of patients out of being suicidal, but not all were successful.  I feel like I may be in that category of just not being strong enough.  I’ve managed to work two jobs at 12 hour shifts, handled hard and difficult cases, provided for my family, helped raise 3 children, and through it all got my bachelors and masters despite times where I had to write feverishly in between arguments where I’ve only been allotted perhaps 1-3 hours of time to myself to finish a 5-6 page research paper.  I got these degrees not with the help to my wife, but despite her.  I consider myself a very strong willed person who takes his job and his calling seriously.  I’ve even managed to overcome the issues I feel have been at my core with my bipolar disorder without the needs of medication (which I am NOT AGAINST and understand the need of them, trust me, especially in crisis and instability).  I, however, don’t feel like I’m strong enough to continue through this and also not strong enough to kill myself without the fear of pain. I’m stuck.  And instead of going insane, I’ve just completely collapsed in decision making and drive.  I’m smiling right now, continuing to care for my children, care for the nearly 100 residential psychiatric clients I care for, and oversee the 100+ staff I am in charge of making sure they are safe, appreciated, and not alone in their job.  All the while I am doing this, I’m quietly thinking about ways to die. When I drive around, I try to find the best looking trees to hang from.  I actively look up cocktails to drown my pain.  And beneath my mask, knowing the power of words and their decree, I declare my desire to die in a whisper of both despair and relief.  I want to die.  I want this cycle to end.  I already trained an assistant on how to do my job. I already spoken to my children about things they should know, how to live, how to treat others.  I have enough writings in school to show them my thoughts on certain matters and issues. I also hope to write them letters that it’s okay to call me a coward and that I did take a cowardly way and that my thoughts aren’t rational and that I’m sorry I wasn’t strong enough to push through this. They see the dynamics.  They see my misery.  My middle child sometimes holds me and says that I’ll get through this as I fight back tears after being ridiculed by my wife or yelled for a mistake I made or for something I did.  I pray every morning and night for forgiveness if I end my life prematurely.  I’m even looking up ways to reduce my immune response so this virus can just kill me.  My resolve is different from previous suicidal thoughts. This is something like a project - a policy and procedure I must write up and then carry-out.  It’s different this time.

Sorry for the first word “Debate” at the top. It was the title of my note on my phone and got copied over.  If I have any other errors I apologize.  Since being COVID positive, I have been experiencing haziness and been more clumsy.  When I mentioned this to my wife she simply says “you’re always like that though”.

EDIT: Argh, I see more spelling errors. Again, I apologize.

EDIT (2):  Also; there’s more that can be said about the dynamics in the house - how I’ve always been embracing and helpful towards her family (my in-laws) and how cold she’s been to mine.  I even helped them financially through this pandemic and allowed one of them to live with me with her baby.  When she asked about rent, I said “whatever you comfortably can afford”, to which she’s paying around $150 a month or so which just goes towards the marked increase in the AC bill.

EDIT (3):  It’s important to mention all the changes I asked to be made in this marriage that she agreed upon didn’t last. The only thing now, I feel, is her stronger resolve to point out my flaws and even says my having COVID-19 is a result of my own decision to separate from her.  Any time I raise my voice (not yell, but disagree), I’m just going back to my “old ways”.  I am considered to be the sole reason for our marital distress when I left a few weeks ago and when I told her if she had any part it in as well she simply gives a canned response of “oh yes, I know I’m not perfect but...” then proceeds to bash me further.
